style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a weathered concrete surface, extreme asymmetry, off-centre layout. A small, sleek brushed steel input module sits on the left, connected via heavy interlocking structural ribbons to a massive, towering stack of dark matte polymer processing bays that dominate the right side of the frame. Hard clean edges, one directional key light throwing a long, heavy cast shadow to the left, generous negative space. Matte muted palette with a single amber accent on the large stack, no text or moulded lettering.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, watermark, UI, typography, garbled, bare shapes, abstract cubes
rationale: A component assembly visually builds the concept of hidden bloat by showing a small, seemingly efficient module physically dragging a massive, hidden structural burden behind it, using stark scale contrast.
subject: modular mechanical assembly with a small input block tethered to a massive stack of opaque processing bays
core_thesis: Output tokens are billed at a multiple of the input rate and the reasoning half of them is invisible, meaning a tier priced 50% cheaper per token can cost 57% more per resolved task.
core_conflict: Lower sticker price for input tokens vs invisible, uncontrollable output token bloat.
